title: Steer the curriculum
summary: Levels climb on their own as runners master them. Your script can pick the level, the number of courses and the bar for moving up.

steps.title: Start on the spikes
steps.body:
A curriculum is a list of lessons for the population, easiest first. Every generation runs fresh courses of the current level, and the level goes up once the best runners finish most of them.

The each generation block can change that. `useLevel` trains the next generation on another level, and the curriculum carries on from there.

Move the run to level 3 after its first generation. The check trains 2 generations and reports the highest level it saw.
hints: generation counts from 0, so if generation == 0 runs once, after the first generation.
Write if generation == 0 { useLevel(level: 3) } inside each generation.

steps.title: More courses per brain
steps.body:
Each brain runs two courses per generation by default, and its score is the average. A brain can get lucky on one room, but rarely on three.

`coursesPerGeneration` sets the count, from 1 to 4. More courses judge brains more fairly, but each generation takes longer. Ask for 3.

check.message: Call coursesPerGeneration in the each generation block.

hints: It takes one argument named count.

steps.title: Your own bar
steps.body:
The level goes up once the best fifth of the population finish 75% of their courses over two generations. The best fifth breed the next generation, so their score is what counts.

`autoLevel` sets a bar of your own. A higher bar means more practice on each level before the next. Set it to 0.9.

In the lab, the Progress tab shows the level climb and both finish shares, so you can watch your bar at work.

check.message: Call autoLevel in the each generation block.

hints: It takes one argument named threshold, from 0.05 to 1.
